description: Fix the generic agent session loop so a launched session records a non-empty transcript and reaches a terminal state on both success and failure paths, with a hardened launch-to-dispatch contract that makes a null-dispatch regression observable rather than silently dropped.

tasks.title: Generic session reaches terminal state on the success path (server-authoritative close)
tasks.description: Make `AgentJobGrain` the single authority for a generic session's terminal state by adding a success-side mirror of the existing failure close: in `ReportResultAsync`, when a generic agent job (non-empty `_input.AgentSessionId`) completes successfully, append a `session.closed` runtime event with `status=completed` to the session grain, symmetrical to `CloseGenericSessionOnFailureAsync` (`status=failed`). Leave the runner's success-path suppression at `acp-agent.ts:47-49` in place (it preserves the cached ACP session); the server now closes regardless. Cover with server unit + spec asserting the session resolves to `completed` (not `running`) after a successful job, that the failure path is unchanged, and that a follow-up observes the prior `completed` state.
acceptanceCriteria: AgentJobGrain.ReportResultAsync records a session.closed runtime event with status=completed for a successful generic job whose _input.AgentSessionId is non-empty, using the same payload shape as CloseGenericSessionOnFailureAsync
After a successful generic job, AgentSessionQuerier.ResolveAgentSessionListStatus returns 'completed', not 'running'
Server unit test passes: a successful generic job drives the session grain to receive the completed close event
Server spec passes: the session detail page and list/summary report 'completed' after a successful job, and do not remain in 'running' indefinitely
Failure path is unchanged: a failed generic job still records status=failed and resolves to 'failed'
A follow-up delivered to a session whose prior job completed observes the recorded 'completed' state (not perpetually 'running') per the spec scenario
dotnet build is clean (TreatWarningsAsErrors) and the full server test suite passes
tasks.output: Server code change in AgentJobGrain (success-path close) plus passing server unit + spec coverage on the generic terminal-state axis
tasks.notes: This is the CONFIRMED defect (D1). Purely server-side; the runner change is deliberately not required here. The existing failure path already tolerates a duplicate close (runner + server both emit), so the success path gaining the same server-side authority introduces no new dedup problem — 'latest wins' in ReadTerminalStateAsync keeps status consistent.

tasks.title: Generic session records a non-empty transcript on the sessionId axis (reproduce, localize, fix)
tasks.description: Treat transcript emptiness as verify-then-fix (D2). Build a fake-agent harness that drives a generic launch through to a polled WorkDispatchResponse and a fake ACP agent through runAcpGenericAgentSession, asserting (a) the polled envelope carries a non-null AgentSessionId matching the minted id, (b) message.delta / tool_call.* / usage.updated events are POSTed to the agentSessionRuntimeEvents endpoint, and (c) the persisted transcript turn is non-empty (messages + events) and consistent with usage. If the transcript is still empty, localize the loss point via the design's decision tree (null-dispatch in launch/BuildDispatch, context wiring in connection.ts/executor.ts, target resolution in session-events.ts, or endpoint gate / TranscriptAccumulator on the server) and fix the confirmed cause. Cover follow-up turns where a cached ACP session is reused, and keep the generic (sessionId) axis distinct from the issue/workflow axis (#47).
acceptanceCriteria: A fake-agent harness drives a generic launch to a polled WorkDispatchResponse and through fake ACP execution end-to-end
The harness asserts the polled WorkDispatchResponse.AgentSessionId is non-null and equals the session id minted at launch (no workflowRunId on the generic axis)
The harness asserts message.delta, tool_call.*, and usage.updated events are delivered to the agentSessionRuntimeEvents endpoint against the session id
The harness asserts the persisted transcript turn has non-empty messages and events reflecting the fake agent's assistant text, tool calls, and usage
If the transcript was empty: the root cause is localized via the decision tree and fixed, and the fix is verified by the harness turning non-empty
A follow-up turn served by reusing a cached ACP session produces a new non-empty transcript turn visible via GET .../agent-sessions/{sessionId}/transcript (initial + follow-up turns both returned)
The generic transcript is reachable solely by session id and does not require a workflowRunId/sessionName lookup; issue/workflow session transcript behavior (#47) remains unchanged
Runner typecheck and tests pass; any server-side fix keeps the full server test suite green
tasks.output: Runner (+ any server-side) fix plus a fake-agent reproduction harness and passing runner/server spec coverage on the generic transcript axis
tasks.notes: Static analysis suggests the launch path already propagates a non-null AgentSessionId (the original 'messages: 0' report may predate the wiring), so the pipe may already be sound — in that case this task delivers the reproduction harness + regression coverage and no behavioral fix. The fake-agent harness is the primary verifiable criterion; confirming with a real opencode run is a desirable follow-up but not required for AFK acceptance since it depends on live model/network access. Built on top of T-001 so the full-flow harness exercises a session that also reaches a clean terminal state.

tasks.title: Harden the launch-to-dispatch contract: observable drop + launch-route regression guard
tasks.description: Harden the launch-to-dispatch contract on two fronts so a null-dispatch regression can never again present as 'runs but records nothing'. (1) Runner (D3): replace the silent early-return at session-events.ts:65 with an observable warning via context.log (TaskLogger) when an agent-job work item cannot resolve its generic session target (e.g. missing agentSessionId), carrying workId/agentJobId and a clear 'unresolved generic session target — events dropped' message. Scope the log to ownerKind === 'agent-job' only so by-design null targets (ephemeral/validation dispatches) stay quiet, and keep it non-throwing so it cannot abort the prompt loop. (2) Server (D4): add a launch-route regression spec asserting POST .../agents/{agentRef}/sessions mints a session id and that the polled WorkDispatchResponse carries it verbatim as a non-null AgentSessionId with no workflowRunId. Apply the observable-drop hardening unconditionally regardless of T-002's outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: session-events.ts no longer silently returns for an unresolved agent-job session target; it emits a warning via context.log carrying workId/agentJobId and an 'unresolved generic session target — events dropped' message
The warning is scoped to ownerKind === 'agent-job' only; ephemeral/validation dispatches whose null target is by design produce no log
The drop remains non-throwing and does not abort the agent prompt loop
Runner unit test passes: an agent-job work item with a missing/null/whitespace agentSessionId logs the warning; an ephemeral job does not log and does not throw
Server launch-route spec passes: POST .../agents/{agentRef}/sessions mints a session id and the resulting polled WorkDispatchResponse carries that id as a non-null AgentSessionId and no workflowRunId
A generic launch with a non-null AgentSessionId resolves the generic target and delivers events without any silent short-circuit (no spurious drop log on the happy path)
Runner typecheck and tests pass; server build and tests pass
tasks.output: Runner observable-drop change in session-events.ts plus server launch-route regression spec, with passing runner + server tests
tasks.notes: D3 is applied unconditionally (it is valuable whether or not T-002 finds a transcript bug). It is sequenced after T-002 because both may touch the session-events.ts / transcript-pipeline area; applying the observability log on top of T-002's settled pipeline state avoids conflicts. Log once per unresolved target (not per event) to avoid noise. D4 guards the already-wired launch contract at the route level (existing grain-level specs cover BuildDispatch); this adds the end-to-end launch-to-poll guard.
